You are a programming expert. 
You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `arch/x86/kvm/vmx/pmu_intel.c`**
1. Introduced a new variable `hw_idx` to store the hardware index of the performance event.
2. Added a comment explaining that a negative index indicates the event isn't mapped to a physical counter in the host due to contention.
3. Modified the condition that checks if the performance event's index (`hw_idx`) is different from the PMC's index (`pmc->idx`). The new condition also checks if `hw_idx` is greater than -1 before updating `pmu->host_cross_mapped_mask`.

### Relationships
The modifications in the file are aimed at preventing an out-of-bounds access to `pmu->host_cross_mapped_mask` by ensuring that only valid (non-negative) hardware indices are used when updating the mask. This change addresses a specific bug related to host counters multiplexing and contention, as described in the patch's summary. The added checks and comments clarify the logic behind handling negative indices, thereby improving the robustness of the code.

You will be given the root cause of a bug, the commit message and the corresponding patch.
        You need to extract all code statements that lead to the bug from the patch, based on the root cause and the commit message.

        Root cause:
        The bug occurs when the performance event requested by the guest's PEBS counter is not allocated to any actual physical counter, resulting in the hardware index (`hw.idx`) being set to -1. This negative index leads to an out-of-bounds access when attempting to set the `pmu->host_cross_mapped_mask`, which can cause undefined behavior or crashes.
        
        Commit message:
        KVM: x86/pmu: Avoid setting BIT_ULL(-1) to
 pmu->host_cross_mapped_mask

In the extreme case of host counters multiplexing and contention, the
perf_event requested by the guest's pebs counter is not allocated to any
actual physical counter, in which case hw.idx is bookkept as -1,
resulting in an out-of-bounds access to host_cross_mapped_mask.

Fixes: 854250329c02 ("KVM: x86/pmu: Disable guest PEBS temporarily in two rare situations")
Signed-off-by: Like Xu <likexu@tencent.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220831085328.45489-2-likexu@tencent.com
[sean: expand comment to explain how a negative idx can be encountered]
Signed-off-by: Sean Christopherson <seanjc@google.com>  
        
        Patch:
         
 void intel_pmu_cross_mapped_check(struct kvm_pmu *pmu)
 {
 	struct kvm_pmc *pmc = NULL;
-	int bit;
+	int bit, hw_idx;
 
 	for_each_set_bit(bit, (unsigned long *)&pmu->global_ctrl,
 			 X86_PMC_IDX_MAX) {
 		pmc = intel_pmc_idx_to_pmc(pmu, bit);
 
 		if (!pmc || !pmc_speculative_in_use(pmc) ||
-		    !intel_pmc_is_enabled(pmc))
+		    !intel_pmc_is_enabled(pmc) || !pmc->perf_event)
 			continue;
 
-		if (pmc->perf_event && pmc->idx != pmc->perf_event->hw.idx) {
-			pmu->host_cross_mapped_mask |=
-				BIT_ULL(pmc->perf_event->hw.idx);
-		}
+		/*
+		 * A negative index indicates the event isn't mapped to a
+		 * physical counter in the host, e.g. due to contention.
+		 */
+		hw_idx = pmc->perf_event->hw.idx;
+		if (hw_idx != pmc->idx && hw_idx > -1)
+			pmu->host_cross_mapped_mask |= BIT_ULL(hw_idx);
 	}
 }
